summary: Hot September producer-price data revived fears of Fed rate hikes, splitting the market: the Dow and S&P held up while the Nasdaq sank on a deepening AI-trade sell-off. Chip stocks led the slide as worries about debt-financed data-center spending spread, while crude rallied on Middle East shipping risks.
market_note: Rotation day: industrials and energy up, tech and chips down, and the 10-year yield slipping below 5.1%.

items.why: Extending Wednesday's 5.7% slide as AI infrastructure financing fears spread. CoreWeave's bond sell-off and slowing Anthropic revenue growth (per IBD) raised doubts about chip demand, hitting AMD harder than Nvidia.

Crude bid as traders price supply risk after a reported missile strike on a Saudi Aramco building and fresh tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, with tanker freight rates running about nine times last year's level.
Caught in the same AI trade sell-off as AMD as worries over debt-financed data-center spending grew. Reports that Anthropic's revenue growth slowed to 46% from 143% in Q2 added to the pressure.
Under pressure from hot inflation data lifting rate-hike bets, plus traders de-risking ahead of Oct 21 earnings. Tonight's Roadster unveiling event has so far failed to offset the macro selling.
